subject: Feeling scared. Isolated. Ashamed.
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110387672/554182511/-1812448514?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ODEwNDQ3ZS05ODUzLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lMQEBiKKfxUdxwPH3L2RQMK9AXg7wSsatRdHrgKLjgs=)
Peter, Before I came home to Illinois, I was a meteorologist at a local station in Tyler, Texas. One morning, my boss approached me and said we needed to speak after the show. When I got to the conference room, I saw my employment contract laid out on the desk. Next to it was a printout of my profile from a gay dating website. I was told I had a choice: to be _"that person"_ in the profile or "have a job." I decided then and there to resign and move back to Illinois. **That was more than 20 years ago, and the reason I’m sharing this story now is because I never imagined the LGBTQ community would be experiencing such a surge in discrimination since Trump and his allies came into the picture.** We've seen another round of far-right politicians banning books from schools and libraries, and scrubbing entire histories off government websites. Just across our district’s border, our neighbors in Iowa are taking their book ban through the courts. In case it ever needs saying, the people who ban books have never been the good guys. I can tell you for a fact that if I were a kid today watching this, I'd be feeling scared, isolated, and ashamed, as so many groups are right now. **These attacks are a reminder of why we need representatives in Congress who can lead with empathy -- especially when it comes to protecting youth who may already feel marginalized.** [**I’m standing up to hate in Congress, but it's going to take a team effort to get this done. clean_body: | = Peter, Before I came home to Illinois, I was a meteorologist at a local station in Tyler, Texas. One morning, my boss approached me and said we needed to speak after the show. When I got to the conference room, I saw my employment contract laid out on the desk. Next to it was a printout of my profile from a gay dating website. I was told I had a choice: to be "that person" in the profile or "have a job." I decided then and there to resign and move back to Illinois. That was more than 20 years ago, and the reason I’m sharing this story now is because I never imagined the LGBTQ community would be experiencing such a surge in discrimination since Trump and his allies came into the picture. We've seen another round of far-right politicians banning books from schools and libraries, and scrubbing entire histories off government websites. Just across our district’s border, our neighbors in Iowa are taking their book ban through the courts. In case it ever needs saying, the people who ban books have never been the good guys. I can tell you for a fact that if I were a kid today watching this, I'd be feeling scared, isolated, and ashamed, as so many groups are right now. These attacks are a reminder of why we need representatives in Congress who can lead with empathy -- especially when it comes to protecting youth who may already feel marginalized. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thanks for hearing me out, Eric | Eric Sorensen is a meteorologist born and raised in Rockford, IL representing IL-17 in Congress. name: Scott Brown
subject: I have something personal to share with you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Brown for New Hampshire, Inc
body:
Peter,

My name is Scott Brown, and I want to take a few minutes to share my story
with you and how the experiences and lessons I’ve learned have led me to make a
big decision this week.
I had a challenging upbringing. My mom was married and divorced four times,
and my dad was married and divorced three times. I was raised by my single mom,
who worked multiple jobs to put food on the table. We didn’t have much, but
with the love and support of my grandparents, we had a fighting chance. We
moved often—I lived in 17 different places before I turned 18.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
I know what it’s like to worry about where your next meal is coming from or
whether the bills all get paid.And those early years taught me the value of
grit, of resilience, and hard work.

Nothing in my life has ever been handed to me — I’ve had to fight for every
step forward.

I worked my way through college and law school, taking any odd job and doing
whatever it took to stay afloat.

At 19, I joined the Army National Guard. I served for more than 30 years and
retired as a Colonel. I’ve worn our nation’s uniform with pride and know
firsthand what it means to serve a cause bigger than yourself.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
Back in 2010, I took a leap that many thought was crazy. I ran for the U.S.
Senate in Massachusetts as a Republican,driven by a belief that people like you
deserved a real voice in Washington, not just another career politician. I
drove across the state, putting countless miles on my beloved truck, a 2005 GMC
Canyon. With the incredible support of grassroots supporters like you from all
corners of the country,we pulled off a stunning upset and won, shaking the
political establishment to its core.

But that victory was just the start.

I went to Washington as a disruptor, refusing to play the insider games of
career politicians. That made me a target. The national Democrats zeroed in,
recruiting Elizabeth Warren and pouring tens of millions into a campaign to
defeat me. Despite our best efforts, we came up short in that race.

But I wasn’t discouraged. I believed then, and I believe now, that there’s a
bigger plan for all of us.

My wife, Gail, and I became four-time grandparents, and we’ve poured our
hearts into our family and our New Hampshire community. In 2017, when President
Trump asked me to serve as U.S. Ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa,I was
honored to represent our nation, strengthen global partnerships, and protect
American interests abroad.
<https://secure.winred.com/nrsc/doge-hit-ground-running-tc-rs-hf/?recurring=true&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&address=&zip=&city=&state=&employer_name=&occupation=&amtposition=4>

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
Today, I’m writing to you with big news: I’m not done fighting. Our country’s
future is at a crossroads, and I’m stepping up again to run for the U.S. Senate
in New Hampshire.I’m doing this for you, for our shared values, and for the
America we believe in. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
You’ve seen what happens when Democrats hold unchecked power...

Runaway inflation...

Chaos at our southern border...

Soft-on-crime policies...

Men in women’s sports and locker rooms...

Foreign policy missteps that weaken our allies and embolden our enemies.

Hardworking Americans like you are being left behind, and we can’t let this
radical agenda take over the Senate in 2026.The stakes are just too high.

Here’s the truth: I can’t do this without you.

The Democrats and their elite allies will flood this race with MILLIONS. It’s
an open seat in a swing state. They don’t want someone like me—someone who
speaks plainly, serves with honor, and refuses to sell out—anywhere near
Washington.

That’s why I’m reaching out to you today, asking you to stand with me from
Day One.

A contribution of $5, $10, or whatever you can give will help us build a
campaign powered by people like you, not political insiders.
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
Every dollar counts, and every voice matters. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaej_acs&utm_campaign=20250627_bio-launch_sb>
If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter, I’m here to tell you it
does. It matters to me. And it’s the only reason I’m in this fight.

Let’s do this together.

Scott Brown
Candidate for U.S. Senate
New Hampshire Chip in to Join Scott Brown »

name: Melissa Chaudhry from "It's a Matter of Integrity" by Melissa Chaudhry
subject: When a Generation Grows Up in War
body:
What it means that nearly 1 in 5 children live amid conflict--and how we can stop normalizing the crisis.

# [When a Generation Grows Up in War](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=166352558&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTY2MzUyNTU4LCJpYXQiOjE3NTEwNTgzNzAsImV4cCI6MTc1MzY1MDM3MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.JmRHTzKq1Rnhhcd4I1wTbRfEIDv_Gmqh7vik7giBsa0)

### INTRODUCTION
In late 2024, UNICEF sounded the alarm: **473 million children globally--almost one in five--now live in conflict zones**, marking the **highest level of violence against children since[World War II](https://substack.com/redirect/9fe59682-6406-445b-81d1-dc24b69a2a6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. That figure represents a dramatic increase from the roughly 10% of children in conflict areas during the 1990s, nearly doubling to **19%** today.
Alongside this demographic milestone comes another grim record: in 2023, UN-verified "grave violations"--including killings, abductions, and recruitment--affected **22,557 children** , totaling **[32,990 violations](https://substack.com/redirect/17f5ac6e-1108-4006-a186-921354ccac32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. And that was _before_ the genocide in Gaza, in which thousands of children have been [abducted](https://substack.com/redirect/e86a4ed2-5ec4-4a33-b302-77b8651c65f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and many tens of thousands slaughtered.
Each of these children was innocent. Each had hopes, dreams, loves, and potential. Each one, we would have held close and protected and comforted, if given the chance. Can we harness that love and rage and grief, and _make_ more chances to care and protect the most vulnerable, before it's too late?
If we do not respond _systematically_ and _urgently_ when confronting violence against children, we risk normalizing the most visceral and universal evil human beings can face. Harming children _**must be a red line**_ \- whether at home or abroad, whether in a school shooting or an apartment building hit by military weapons.
Let's consider what we're dealing with, when 1 in 5 of the world's children live in conflict zones. Let's look at the long-term consequences, what will be required to help these children heal... and let's consider what we can do to change the conditions that give rise to these statistics -- until we live in a world where **no child** is harmed by adult violence.

* * *
### 1\. THE MULTIFACETED IMPACT ON CHILDREN
#### 🧠 Mental Health Under Siege
Research consistently documents that war-induced trauma inflicts deep psychological wounds.
* Exposure to violence, separation from caregivers, and displacement correlate strongly with **PTSD, depression, and anxiety** , and often **[lifelong psychosocial damage](https://substack.com/redirect/af93be13-8be5-4470-9e0b-1409f9654c87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
* A 2024 scoping review of displaced children found depression, PTSD, anxiety, sleep disorders, nightmares, somatic symptoms, and even signs of substance abuse--not just immediate reactions, but[ enduring conditions](https://substack.com/redirect/2a279fe9-69a2-4a34-9ec1-34fa78102bbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* In Burkina Faso, [10 of 11 children](https://substack.com/redirect/3940d0de-732d-4e64-a3f4-3341fbde604a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) exposed to intense conflict showed trauma signs, yet **mental health services were scarce**.

#### 📚 Education Disruption = Future Disruption
* About **[13 million children](https://substack.com/redirect/de994771-1aaf-4305-bb67-c93384b09feb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are out of school**, and nearly **9,000 schools have been destroyed** --particularly across Middle Eastern conflicts.
* In [Gaza alone](https://substack.com/redirect/0cb9823a-148f-4d03-9b34-2e69359c0e2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), **85% of schools have been hit** ; **600,000 pupils** lost access to education, with over **5,800 students killed** by mid-2024.
* Educational interruptions undermine social-emotional development and contribute to **[a growing"lost generation"](https://substack.com/redirect/b2f80fd8-ec81-4689-a979-f0f58f1519e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.

#### 📉 Human Capital & Intergenerational Damage
* Human capital researchers examining the Anglophone [conflict in Cameroon](https://substack.com/redirect/b7282cd7-547a-4e73-a9e8-b74f34b3ef4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that violence led to measurable drops in reading and math test scores, increased teacher absenteeism, and infrastructure decay.
* Higher childhood exposure to armed conflict correlates with **stunted educational attainment, health, and productivity** --trends that ripple into future generations.

* * *
### 2\. A SYSTEMIC RESPONSE FRAMEWORK
When the scale of suffering is this enormous, simple charity alone won't be enough. To truly change this reality, we need a coordinated, rights-based response that matches the scale of the problem:
#### 📌 A. Elevate Child Protection in International Norms
* Acts like recruiting child soldiers or targeting children in conflict must be treated as **enforceable war crimes** with **real consequences --sanctions, prosecutions, aid restrictions**.
* Key global organizations--UNICEF, OHCHR, UNHCR--need **stronger mandates, resources, and independent investigative powers** in conflict zones.

#### 📌 B. Humanitarian Corridors & Safe Zones for Children
* We must urgently negotiate **child-first evacuation corridors** with trusted neutral actors (like ICRC or faith leaders).
* Regional **Child Safe Zones** should be created in neighboring countries, with access to healthcare, trauma care, education, and community support.

#### 📌 C. Clamp Down on Arms Fueling Conflict
* The **Arms Trade Treaty** must be strengthened and enforced, ensuring accountability for governments that arm those who commit atrocities against children.
* Major arms exporters (US, EU, Russia, China) should require **child protection impact assessments** for all arms transfers.

#### 📌 D. Scale Mental Health, Education, and Trauma Recovery
* Fund **trauma-informed mental health support** at multiple levels: play therapy, school counseling, community-based healing programs.
* Rebuild educational systems with **trauma-aware curricula** and emotional resilience at their core.
* Provide **long-term support** for children and communities--healing after conflict takes years, not months.

#### 📌 E. Address Root Causes: Governance, Development, Resilience
* Real prevention means tackling the drivers of conflict: bad governance, corruption, inequality, climate stress.
* We must invest in **peacebuilding, community-driven development, and resilience programs** that prevent future cycles of violence.

* * *
### 3\. WHY WE CANNOT NORMALIZE THIS
If we accept that **1 in 5 children** should grow up in war zones, we lock in a future of **broken institutions, lost potential, and endless cycles of trauma**.
As UNICEF warns: _" This must not become the new normal."_
These children deserve more than our sympathy. They deserve systems that protect them.
* * *
### 4\. WHAT CAN YOU DO?
It can feel overwhelming, but each of us can be part of the solution. Here are a few ways to start:
**1\. Support organizations on the ground**
Groups like UNICEF, Save the Children, and Doctors Without Borders are providing frontline care to children in conflict. Even small donations make a real difference.
**2\. Raise awareness**
Talk about this issue with your friends, on social media, in your community groups. Keeping attention on these children helps prevent their suffering from being ignored.
**3\. Advocate for change**
Call your elected officials--local and federal--and urge them to prioritize child protection in foreign and domestic policy. Demand accountability for arms exports and a stronger U.S. role in enforcing international norms.
**4\. Get involved in local or international work**
If you're in education, health, law, social work, or public policy--consider applying your skills to child protection or humanitarian advocacy.
**5\. Explore careers in trauma recovery**
The world needs more therapists, counselors, and community workers who are equipped to help children heal from violence. This is a deeply meaningful way to serve.
* * *
No action is too small--and together, many small actions can create the political will, the public demand, and the international momentum we need to stop this crisis.
A better future is possible--for your children, for my children, and for everyone's children--if we choose, commit, and act for it.
No one is coming to save us... and without us, no one is coming to save _**them**_.
Foward, together, in fierce love,
Melissa Chaudhry

body:
An update from Jocelyn’s statewide tour!
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
Greetings from the road, team!
We’re hitting the road across Michigan with Jocelyn on her “Thrive in Michigan Tour.” Our team is traveling around the state, meeting people where they’re at and hearing their stories.
[**Below are some pics from the trail — but before you scroll further, we hope you’ll pitch in a few bucks to help Jocelyn stay on the road and reach more Michiganders!**](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
[DONATE](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=3&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
---
[](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
Our tour started in Traverse City, where we met with the inspiring people at GTI Industries — a company that empowers people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, creating inclusive workplaces where _everyone_ is valued and has the opportunity to succeed.
[](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=5&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
Then we heard from people in Muskegon. Folks shared their hopes, fears, and visions for Michigan — and Jocelyn shared hers. These conversations are how we’ll ensure the policies we amplify actually touch the Michiganders who need it most.
[](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=6&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
We loved our day in Southwest Michigan — one of the most beautiful parts of our state, filled with hardworking people who want the best for their communities. Jocelyn will always show up for the people in Michigan in every corner of the state.
[](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=7&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)
Jocelyn is in this fight for the residents of Wayne County worried about housing and grocery costs, and for every Michigander who wants to thrive, not just survive.
**Every conversation and every stop reminds Jocelyn and our team that our path to a stronger Michigan runs through the people who power it.**
[**Chip in to help Jocelyn stay on the road, having more conversations with Michiganders and sharing her vision for Michigan’s future!**](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/239?c0=jmb-em-q22025.rGq0NW&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250627_PM1_V1_S1&t=8&akid=454%2E181023%2EROGRGB)

# DeSantis says "Alligator Alcatraz" to hold criminal aliens as early as Tuesday
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled a new high-security immigration detention facility dubbed **["Alligator Alcatraz"](https://substack.com/redirect/3c757f23-423a-48ff-bcea-4fc7bcae776d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** designed to support the Trump administration's deportation efforts.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/df072dec-038f-4d76-9d31-59832b58501e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **DeSantis gave** _**Fox & Friends**_**co-host Steve Doocy a tour** of the new deportation facility, approved by the Trump administration Tuesday to process and detain illegal immigrants. "Obviously, you have ICE operations but that is not enough and so there needs to be more ability to intake process and deport and so this answers that," DeSantis told the Fox reporter.
* **The facility can process over 3,000 detainees** and includes a runway to facilitate direct deportation flights -- a "one-stop shop" according to the Florida governor.
* **DeSantis emphasized the state 's full support of federal immigration enforcement,** stating that the new center enhances DHS and ICE capabilities and relieves pressure on local law enforcement.
_" If a criminal alien escapes, you have nowhere to go," DeSantis said. "What are you going to do? Trudge through the swamp and dodge alligators 50 or 60 miles to civilization? Not going to happen."_
* **The governor highlighted the facility 's remote, swampy location** as a deterrent to escape, claiming it adds to security while minimizing impact on Florida residents. The project was built by Florida's Division of Energy Management, who DeSantis credits for the facility's timely creation.

# SCOTUS rules in favor of parental rights to decide if child is exposed to LGBTQ content in school
The Supreme Court **[ruled in favor of parents](https://substack.com/redirect/dfbbe012-3c7c-4814-963a-a9eab0e0a73e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** calling for opt-outs of woke LGBTQ curriculums in elementary schools based on religious beliefs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dfbbe012-3c7c-4814-963a-a9eab0e0a73e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **6 -3 Supreme Court Decision**: The Court ruled in a 6-3 vote that parents in Montgomery County, Maryland, may opt their children out of elementary school lessons featuring LGBTQ-themed books.
* **Religious Freedom at the Core** : Parents--including Muslim, Roman Catholic, and Ukrainian Orthodox faiths--argued their religious beliefs were infringed when the school district eliminated opt-out options in March 2023. Justice Alito, writing for the majority, emphasized that compelling children to attend such lessons burdens parental free exercise. "A government burdens the religious exercise of parents when it requires them to submit their children to instruction that poses 'a very real threat of undermining' the religious beliefs and practices that the parents wish to instill," Justice Alito wrote.
* **Concerns Over Administrative Burden** : Dissenting Justice Sotomayor warned that the ruling could lead to chaos for schools, requiring them to identify and notify parents of any LGBTQ-related content--potentially undermining public education and inclusive curricula.
* **Case Still Ongoing** : The ruling grants a **preliminary injunction** and sends the case back to lower courts for further proceedings. It's not yet a final judgment on the broader policy, meaning legal review continues.

Religious Freedom at the Core : Parents--including Muslim, Roman Catholic, and Ukrainian Orthodox faiths--argued their religious beliefs were infringed when the school district eliminated opt-out options in March 2023. Justice Alito, writing for the majority, emphasized that compelling children to attend such lessons burdens parental free exercise. "A government burdens the religious exercise of parents when it requires them to submit their children to instruction that poses 'a very real threat of undermining' the religious beliefs and practices that the parents wish to instill," Justice Alito wrote. Concerns Over Administrative Burden : Dissenting Justice Sotomayor warned that the ruling could lead to chaos for schools, requiring them to identify and notify parents of any LGBTQ-related content--potentially undermining public education and inclusive curricula. Case Still Ongoing : The ruling grants a preliminary injunction and sends the case back to lower courts for further proceedings. It's not yet a final judgment on the broader policy, meaning legal review continues. body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
All of us here on Team Lizzie know it’s been a tough week for those of us who care deeply about what is happening in our country. Between the Supreme Court decisions announced this week, the terrible bill making its way on Capitol Hill, and the daily insanity from the Trump administration, it can feel like too much.
But we also know how important it is to hold onto hope and keep working for progress. After all, that’s what got us here in the first place—seeing the possibility of what we could do and signing up to do it. And we say "do our best" because—let’s be honest—staying positive in this moment isn’t always easy!
So, before we ask you to contribute toward our end-of-quarter fundraising goal before Monday’s FEC deadline [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe250627?refcode=lpfe250627] , we want to follow our own advice and share a few bright spots from this month:
* More than 5 million people in over 2,100 towns and cities took part in the “No Kings Day” protests, one of the largest protests in American history, sending a clear message against President Trump’s actions and policies.

* President Trump’s net approval rating has plummeted because Lizzie and House Democrats are working with people across the country to make sure people know how harmful his policies are. Two recent polls show it at the lowest level of his second term—proof that what we’re doing is working.

* Democracy Summer has officially kicked off, and we are helping the next generation pick up the baton in this relay. We’re proud to be part of this internship program, helping train and inspire the next generation of political organizers and leaders.
We hope this good news brings a little light to your day—because it certainly helps us stay motivated to keep up the fight.
Now, here’s where you come in: Can you make a contribution to help us reach our end-of-quarter goal before the FEC deadline on Monday? Every dollar helps us stand strong against Texas Republicans’ dangerous threats to redraw our Congressional maps—and gives us the resources we need to organize, connect with voters, and win in what are sure to be tough but winnable elections next year. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe250627?refcode=lpfe250627]
Thanks for standing with Lizzie and for staying positive with us.
Team Lizzie

Fellow Conservative,

I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan.

I’ve deployed nine times to 70 countries to serve this great country. I never expected to run for the U.S. Senate. But when I returned home and saw what was happening to Minnesota—when I saw the radical left rising—I knew I had to step up.

_**And now I need your help.**_

The same Democratic Socialist movement that just **[hijacked New York City is gaining ground here in the Midwest.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=86a94eedee6e4f058fc0c5a657bc4d6b&_e=V8jwyoWFUKObubjTpwoqONeZAF2zii88GXhj3LK2Rd7Ut6otiwnH5DfFn7ASKr_qPlH8uZWVJxi7t_wScBFOwut9oyb3BdcMqrYszoevYW3hZ_G6GqCZytxb5MubNWf58FTfEtm4QKxzNbjOq7NCtQC3PVcSUYR_d8XU559BXD3XKYi141en0UCvkblg9qx3ASgzvlnkcnMvQATkA_tHv9D70Aq2ZE_cfR8zTamKFW3t111Mx37nBXs-ulAvMqD3Q8tjF6wUft-WBmJ9LiODNn0QmK1oc35KcJWOU1-ioKpVmY7HOjjHvxJb2PikMDkR0DV_AjANSMok_YVBPabqFEx6r7EOdOtWXYxwZEFAYyV0QJWpgci3xQ8_4G19CXtb6bPqoKee_Sq_eBn-5Z3OOWjuwoUBkBwBz4ytEGD1lFCaAsfmRCUiQvfDT3z443jWMHccgfaNwBSnL74L7m1V5isUwgNHpr-pWlQs05tNg2uuX7hITVvmmQTqzDT7Yw_iJ9PttpUiF_HVbkX2MhwUy07sq3It6zDliZv8iv4DHtHB5rKs-5YtXK2XQtQFRrmfgzvW-Q4k2GROdNgOXVPMM72rHfEmtTTeCxyRTUuN0OuMplA40uGR3SE_p3rNUKd6wf8_9lhg7MAGgMwQJHGdczKx6H19qR-M1Wa3kXR9nffZ1p0yALBIhMdi_masePnMu3ItaY0VY4SumeBdrsYmsr_OxuYWnABmFwIe0uQ6CbQ%3D) **This week, New York Democrats nominated a man so extreme that he promised to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister and replace city police with social workers. If that sounds insane, it is.

_**But don’t think it’s limited to the coasts.**_****

My opponent—the lieutenant governor of Minnesota—isn’t far behind. She openly aligned with violent unrest in 2020, **pushed to dismantle our police, and filed lawsuits against law enforcement as our communities burned. While Governor Walz tried to save face, she doubled down on chaos.**

This kind of radicalism isn’t an outlier anymore. It’s the new blueprint of the left. And if we don’t draw the line in Minnesota, it will keep spreading.

The Minnesota I grew up in—where you respected your neighbors, honored your country, and stood for law and order—feels like it’s slipping away.

**I didn’t wait to serve my country after 9/11. I enlisted on my 18th birthday and spent over 20 years protecting American freedom abroad. Now I’m fighting to protect it at home. **

I don’t come from money or a political legacy. I come from grit, faith, and a calling to serve. That’s what drives me now.

_**It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us.

[**HELP ME STOP SOCIALISM IN MINNESOTA**](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=86a94eedee6e4f058fc0c5a657bc4d6b&_e=V8jwyoWFUKObubjTpwoqONeZAF2zii88GXhj3LK2Rd7Ut6otiwnH5DfFn7ASKr_qPlH8uZWVJxi7t_wScBFOwut9oyb3BdcMqrYszoevYW3hZ_G6GqCZytxb5MubNWf58FTfEtm4QKxzNbjOq7NCtQC3PVcSUYR_d8XU559BXD3XKYi141en0UCvkblg9qx3ASgzvlnkcnMvQATkA_tHv9D70Aq2ZE_cfR8zTamKFW3t111Mx37nBXs-ulAvMqD3O11Q_QV8Sh1kdsJEiE3XnjzANkMKDgAcGitvLppue9jHO7F-angB9OzxweLjmq00ocFj6kRNApoUNz29-u8si-EK2u-zXzVF12lSLQI8WAMq-XKr-u_X3C0nrGy9BQ4sUQkWdcgEhNzUUFjB8WX8-5eSXicApfHPBoQfsIjt71r5CXiz1NgkneR2uPsL7XYw4jcqD80m6fe-wVR92fuv0oYsxC7B9PI8_3At_ZnNi0JnGeQVYrYks4LjbilStTMrzEfHGNyn9jfzeG7B_6LXTJe4oVFNDIcZB59aQCYRTFxv58Fh_Y5x5FL9o5x8m7es98oAjPnUst4sFaisCIqVtJXBuw55ZGuEm3I570iPO1sFhOHPV17pS6QUdxrM0PEgZ7gUqY-KOqXoUmzHAOm-0dQMRJrFHJtY1zfsVZ5zdSu0mq9Bs5klZiiC93YPlnLyt7DEKFlf6liS1wavWhf5HlTIqPRw6WAWbOEjhFgSuuA%3D) **_

This election isn’t just about one Senate seat. It’s about stopping a national wave of socialist extremism that threatens to bankrupt small businesses, rewrite our values, and destroy what millions of Americans fought and died to defend.

New York may have fallen to it. **But Minnesota doesn’t have to.**

If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter anymore, it does. The radical left is organized, loud, and well-funded. But they don’t speak for most of us.

clean_body: It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. | Fellow Conservative, I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan. I’ve deployed nine times to 70 countries to serve this great country. I never expected to run for the U.S. Senate. But when I returned home and saw what was happening to Minnesota—when I saw the radical left rising—I knew I had to step up. And now I need your help. The same Democratic Socialist movement that just This week, New York Democrats nominated a man so extreme that he promised to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister and replace city police with social workers. If that sounds insane, it is. But don’t think it’s limited to the coasts.** My opponent—the lieutenant governor of Minnesota—isn’t far behind. She openly aligned with violent unrest in 2020, pushed to dismantle our police, and filed lawsuits against law enforcement as our communities burned. While Governor Walz tried to save face, she doubled down on chaos. This kind of radicalism isn’t an outlier anymore. It’s the new blueprint of the left. And if we don’t draw the line in Minnesota, it will keep spreading. The Minnesota I grew up in—where you respected your neighbors, honored your country, and stood for law and order—feels like it’s slipping away. I didn’t wait to serve my country after 9/11. I enlisted on my 18th birthday and spent over 20 years protecting American freedom abroad. Now I’m fighting to protect it at home. I don’t come from money or a political legacy. I come from grit, faith, and a calling to serve. That’s what drives me now. It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. This election isn’t just about one Senate seat. It’s about stopping a national wave of socialist extremism that threatens to bankrupt small businesses, rewrite our values, and destroy what millions of Americans fought and died to defend. New York may have fallen to it. But Minnesota doesn’t have to. If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter anymore, it does. The radical left is organized, loud, and well-funded. But they don’t speak for most of us. We need a new kind of leadership—rooted in service, not self-interest. If you’re not ready to donate today, that’s okay. **BREAKING NEWS:
“Supreme Court to rehear major Louisiana redistricting case”
— The Hill**
Peter, this morning, the U.S. Supreme Court did not issue a decision on _Louisiana v. Callais_ , the Louisiana redistricting case — instead, it ordered the case to be re-argued during the next term.
**For now, the state’s current, Voting Rights Act-compliant map remains in place.**
**But the fight for fair representation continues in Louisiana and across the country as anti-democracy forces keep trying to dilute voters’ power.**
While this case proceeds, we’ll continue to monitor it closely to prepare for all potential outcomes. But judicial battles aren’t the only way to deliver a more representative democracy.
Our movement will keep working from the court house steps to community meetings, from legislative hearings to the ballot box — with a multi-pronged approach that includes organizing people for key fights where free and fair elections are on the line.

It’s rare for a case to be re-argued before the Supreme Court like this, but re-arguments often involve important issues. Significant examples include _Citizens United_ , _Roe v. Wade_ , and _Brown v. Board of Education_.
**_Louisiana v. Callais_ , in addition to deciding the future of the state’s congressional map, could determine the fate of critical protections under the Voting Rights Act (VRA).**
The state’s current, VRA-compliant congressional districts ensure fair representation for all Louisianans. Black voters, who make up about a third of the state’s population, have the opportunity to elect a candidate of their choice in two of Louisiana’s six congressional districts — a hard-won victory after our affiliate, the National Redistricting Foundation, supported a group of voters who successfully challenged a previous map for violating the VRA. **But the new, representative map is still under threat as this case continues — so we must keep organizing.**
**We’ll keep you updated on what happens next. And no matter the outcome, we’ll keep working to ensure a truly representative democracy that gives every voter an equal chance to make their voice heard.**

clean_body: The fight goes on for fair maps and fair representation in Louisiana. | BREAKING NEWS: “Supreme Court to rehear major Louisiana redistricting case” — The Hill Peter, this morning, the U.S. Supreme Court did not issue a decision on Louisiana v. Callais , the Louisiana redistricting case — instead, it ordered the case to be re-argued during the next term. For now, the state’s current, Voting Rights Act-compliant map remains in place. But the fight for fair representation continues in Louisiana and across the country as anti-democracy forces keep trying to dilute voters’ power. While this case proceeds, we’ll continue to monitor it closely to prepare for all potential outcomes. But judicial battles aren’t the only way to deliver a more representative democracy. Our movement will keep working from the court house steps to community meetings, from legislative hearings to the ballot box — with a multi-pronged approach that includes organizing people for key fights where free and fair elections are on the line. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = It’s rare for a case to be re-argued before the Supreme Court like this, but re-arguments often involve important issues. Significant examples include Citizens United , Roe v. Wade , and Brown v. Board of Education. Louisiana v. Callais , in addition to deciding the future of the state’s congressional map, could determine the fate of critical protections under the Voting Rights Act (VRA). The state’s current, VRA-compliant congressional districts ensure fair representation for all Louisianans. Black voters, who make up about a third of the state’s population, have the opportunity to elect a candidate of their choice in two of Louisiana’s six congressional districts — a hard-won victory after our affiliate, the National Redistricting Foundation, supported a group of voters who successfully challenged a previous map for violating the VRA. But the new, representative map is still under threat as this case continues — so we must keep organizing. We’ll keep you updated on what happens next. And no matter the outcome, we’ll keep working to ensure a truly representative democracy that gives every voter an equal chance to make their voice heard. = Thank you, All On The Line Team is the grassroots advocacy campaign supported by the National Redistricting Action Fund. | I never set out to be a politician. I wanted to be a doctor — and became one. I studied medicine and public health and became the youngest health official in a major U.S. city at 30. But I learned something pretty quickly: while a doctor can prescribe medicine to help sick people get better, you can’t prescribe away poverty. You can’t cure what corporate greed does to us in a political system that’s rigged to put profits over people. It's no longer about left versus right — it's about the very top against the rest of us. That’s why I’m running. When I ran in 2018, I kept saying something that people didn’t want to believe at the time: Donald Trump, himself, wasn’t the disease. He was just the symptom of the disease. What’s the disease? Our corrupted politics. Billionaires and mega-corporations are doing more than poisoning our air and water. They’re poisoning our democracy. They use their power to jack up prices, screwing over workers, and driving our costs through the roof. Then, they use their profits to buy access to politicians, leaving our political system too compromised to stop them. That’s the disease that Donald Trump is a symptom of. And our campaign – you, me, our vision for change – is the antidote. Things aren’t going to get better until we take our country back from the billionaires and corporations who are rigging our economy and our politics. And let’s be honest. Right now, the truth is, there aren’t enough leaders in the Senate who are willing to stand up and fight. But it’s not just about fighting back. It’s about what we fight for. Fighting for us is what I’ve done my entire career — whether it was to erase $700 million in medical debt, to test every Detroit school for lead after the Flint water crisis, or to hold corporate polluters accountable. Together, we'll take our fight to Washington. We’ll refuse the terms set by the oligarchs, raise the minimum wage, and fight to bring down costs, protect Social Security and Medicaid for every Michigander, and champion Medicare for All to guarantee every American affordable, accessible healthcare. This is a campaign to change our politics, not just win an election. But first, we need to come out on top in this competitive race — and I can’t do it alone. name: Wes Moore
subject: The racial wealth gap
body:
Let me explain.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=230%2E1086043%2EWi0UvY)
Peter, the only way to reverse bad policy choices is with good policy choices.
Policies that fix the foundation of what’s broken. And that’s what we’re doing here in Maryland.
We know the racial wealth gap affects all of us. It hurts our economy, it restrains job growth, and it limits our potential as a state.
That’s why, since taking office, we’ve invested more than $1.3 billion into our historically black colleges and universities.
We’ve directed over $816 million in procurement awards to Black-owned businesses.
We issued 182,000 pardons to Marylanders for convictions and cannabis possession.
And, just this month, we designated 419 Just Communities to direct up to $400 million in state investments directly to those impacted by exclusionary policies like redlining.
**Our work to close the racial wealth gap -- and expand access to work, wages, and wealth for Black Marylanders -- will continue long past the month of June.**
But I am proud of what we’ve accomplished so far. We’re not only growing Maryland's economy, we’re making it more inclusive.
This work is important, and I’m glad you’re with us.
Elevate,
Wes

clean_body: Let me explain. Peter, the only way to reverse bad policy choices is with good policy choices. Policies that fix the foundation of what’s broken. And that’s what we’re doing here in Maryland. We know the racial wealth gap affects all of us. It hurts our economy, it restrains job growth, and it limits our potential as a state. That’s why, since taking office, we’ve invested more than $1.3 billion into our historically black colleges and universities. We’ve directed over $816 million in procurement awards to Black-owned businesses. We issued 182,000 pardons to Marylanders for convictions and cannabis possession. And, just this month, we designated 419 Just Communities to direct up to $400 million in state investments directly to those impacted by exclusionary policies like redlining. Our work to close the racial wealth gap -- and expand access to work, wages, and wealth for Black Marylanders -- will continue long past the month of June. But I am proud of what we’ve accomplished so far. We’re not only growing Maryland's economy, we’re making it more inclusive. This work is important, and I’m glad you’re with us. Elevate, Wes Wes is able to make this historic progress because of the support of folks like you.

Mick Mulvaney is the former White House Chief of Staff and former Director of OMB in President Trump's first administration. Mick takes us inside the Senate to discuss what modifications the Senate will make and who will vote no based on the current bill. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is putting forth his best effort to get the bill through the Senate. Once passed, it will head to the House, where Speaker Mike Johnson will most likely put the bill up for a vote. If the House votes immediately and it passes it will be on the president's desk by July 4th. Dr. Alberto Martinez is a Professor of History at the University of Texas. While Dr. Martinez has not always been a fan of President Trump, he is a fan of the truth. As Dr. Martinez was preparing his history lessons, he would frequently watch the news. What he noticed was that nearly every story about President Trump was an exaggeration, misrepresentation or just all out fiction. We are here to give you expert insight into how deliberations will go in the Senate and the House. Mick Mulvaney is the former White House Chief of Staff and former Director of OMB in President Trump's first administration. Mick takes us inside the Senate to discuss what modifications the Senate will make and who will vote no based on the current bill. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is putting forth his best effort to get the bill through the Senate. Once passed, it will head to the House, where Speaker Mike Johnson will most likely put the bill up for a vote. If the House votes immediately and it passes it will be on the president's desk by July 4th. Dr. Alberto Martinez is a Professor of History at the University of Texas. While Dr. Martinez has not always been a fan of President Trump, he is a fan of the truth. As Dr. Martinez was preparing his history lessons, he would frequently watch the news. What he noticed was that nearly every story about President Trump was an exaggeration, misrepresentation or just all out fiction. In Dr. Martinez's book The Media Vs The Apprentice, takes us all the way back to the 90's to fact check and debunk the media lies about President Trump. What he shares with us today is shocking!

Hey, this is Vivek Ramaswamy, and I'd like to share a personal story with you.
When I was in middle school, my father got laid off from his factory job at the General Electric plant in Evendale, Ohio. He was one of the hardest workers there, but like thousands of other good men and women, he was laid off without warning.
Most people would complain, whine, and stomp their feet, saying, "It's not fair!".
But not MY dad. He didn't cry about victimhood or racism.
Instead, he picked himself up, dusted himself off, got a new job, and enrolled in night school law classes for the next four years.
But because money was tight, he and my mother couldn't afford childcare. Every day after middle school, my dad would pick me up and we'd drive for 45 minutes to the University of Kentucky across the river.
I'd sit in the back of his law school classes every night.
Most kids my age would hate the idea of spending all day at school just to go to ANOTHER school at night. But not me.
I was FASCINATED, learning about the Constitution, the principles of law, and Supreme Court decisions.
So why do I even share this story with you in the first place?
Because that time in my life taught me a lesson I've never forgotten: Every hardship is an opportunity - if you're willing to work for it.
That mindset is the foundation of my campaign.
I don't believe in a culture of victimhood. I believe in the American Dream. I believe in merit over DEI. In hard work over handouts. In family, faith, and responsibility, not grievance and blame.
Right now, we have a real opportunity to reverse Radical Leftist policies. An opportunity to show how the nuclear family is the best form of governance. An opportunity to showcase how capitalism lifts people out of poverty. An opportunity to reinstate the American Dream.
And I know that you're one of the dedicated American Patriots who believe in that vision.
That's why I need you with me, Fellow American.
[If you can, please consider donating $10 to my campaign for governor today. I need all the help I can get to restore the American Dream for Ohioans and Americans alike.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=bdd21afed2af4b4bb7ffc3b68fd9a8a5&_e=uahRvWUBqC5GkyJiX75kSDU4hNF9mi8MXJZp0JWsqbnB8OG7Z-_fB2Lv_VJtErF8OBRSpFVq12ZnM--7RaV00foFS8vmZaUbctsh0IwIY3MSj9pCTo2F_SVAdBdCGAvFXr7Tj-v_VBgAdg8pOBfvxgDHOUF6IWDFmD7es4XoP-utJvaVStndqKy75vUeRGhsgHg87-K3zIBTVYE5yQcTYL5bLpsvIRYoF-TnAg0lRb2V2bGtUn7y-Pq6y5g6Dc1NzjKccF_2kYemR5iclnqo6Im-G6NTJNGAtiWBn5hJs2FczDLutQ2D2Nj-djrNWSZfYnocA-Gm3P6sRWm8l2DlLJpZFJ4ot50mOQGFSLtY-PSsLITa3HkIotoZKn8IjnYxE-r6e2U43jnoOtzieNa1gK6KnspKVZPyS9M164zn0sQpuxiGiF8GAm9Wk2OGGt3Ic5jVa78iNpApFTA3RxZh95oPvD-f-YdjRMPxAQfPZZuK589yX1Ud8TtcN0MGV3DP503Zn7KtwLWYb6oNEplBRPFngt4VYvozpeppAKw_rFfQm80nbxCDJgmqeFVNrtuCIiTfhSV3RU9E08gGFVmvFhFavJlc6A7Rt3wWKXDbMFHQNUPHS1CMkGRudF8Fn00I6_v_EFxo--YedPVyn48DwMd3vOB15SoXsd5v3hRXz6HSn8rvtUhVjlV0ygNCXpf1LR35cbxDsAtU95FCCSXo4iYs4kTHCTEZVi4WzCf0d7_BP2qo_snveue4fQhvhKPYYMC77z7wvfvZqM-gDRQvPw%3D%3D)
Don't let our nation turn into one full of victims. Help me turn it into one of victors, just like my dad.
Thanks for your support.
God Bless,**Vivek Ramaswamy

Peter,

**In 2012, my wife faced a pregnancy complication that nearly killed her.

**We were expecting our second child, and for weeks we lived scan to scan, hoping each appointment wouldn't bring the worst.

At 20 weeks, she went into early labor. Our daughter, Addison Michelle, was born too soon.

**We held her for just two hours before she passed away.

****That pain never leaves you.

**But what still keeps me up at night is the simple fact that if the laws in place today had existed then, I would have lost them both.

My wife would have died. My oldest daughter would have grown up without her mother. My son and youngest daughter would never have been born.

My family would be incomplete.

We only survived that moment because we lived in a state where doctors could act, where the law allowed them to save my wife's life.

That is why I speak out on reproductive freedom. Because I have lived the consequences. I know what it means when politicians treat your family like a political football.

**And that 's what's happening again.

**Three years ago this week, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. Yesterday, they ruled against Planned Parenthood, opening the door for more restrictions on abortion access nationwide.

Meanwhile, my opponent, Marie Gluesenkamp Perez voted for a Trump-aligned defense bill that guts reproductive care for service members.

**A bill so extreme that Planned Parenthood withdrew its endorsement of her.

It doesn't look like her colleagues learned the right lesson. This week, it was reported that Mitch McConnell said behind closed doors: "I know a lot of us are hearing from people back home about Medicaid. But they'll get over it." [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110391604/554195728/-2044921950?refcode=2025-06-27-mcconnell&recurring=0&amount=13&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=5baa7e4e-a453-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YmFhN2U0ZS1hNDUzLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jqvNxVZXMalSsMltrJz0pmaLrrbZOrZaBGZ5zXWONSo=) **Republicans are preparing to kick 16 million Americans off their health care. You don't "get over" your mom being kicked out of her nursing home because she can't afford to stay. And you don't "get over" your child being sick because you can't get a doctor's appointment. **Republicans don't seem to care about the very real consequences their policies will have.** I'll tell you this: I'm not about to "get over" the possibility of 16 million people losing their health care coverage, just to fund a tax cut to billionaires. clean_body: Republicans think we won’t care about Medicaid cuts. | | | | Remember when Republican Senator Joni Ernst took heat for saying, "Well, we all are going to die" when defending her party's planned cuts to Medicaid? It doesn't look like her colleagues learned the right lesson. This week, it was reported that Mitch McConnell said behind closed doors: "I know a lot of us are hearing from people back home about Medicaid. But they'll get over it." = Republicans are preparing to kick 16 million Americans off their health care. These cuts will be deadly. And their response? Get over it. Losing health care coverage is not something to "get over." You don't "get over" medical emergencies that you can't afford to address. You don't "get over" your mom being kicked out of her nursing home because she can't afford to stay. And you don't "get over" your child being sick because you can't get a doctor's appointment. Republicans don't seem to care about the very real consequences their policies will have. I'll tell you this: I'm not about to "get over" the possibility of 16 million people losing their health care coverage, just to fund a tax cut to billionaires. And I'm pretty sure the American people won't "get over" their Senators and Representatives voting for the biggest health care reduction in U.S. history. name: Sarah McBride
subject: I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
We must continue to fight for what’s right.
#
Hi, it’s Sarah.
When I was growing up, I couldn’t imagine a future like mine. I worried that the heart of this country wasn’t big enough to love someone like me.
But over the years, I’ve witnessed change that once felt unimaginable — and because of voters in my home state of Delaware and supporters across the country, I became the first openly transgender member elected to Congress last November.
I’ve carried that with me throughout this Pride Month.
**Because Pride teaches us that hope matters most when it’s hard.**
Right now, it’s a frightening time for so many in our country. LGBTQ+ people, especially trans youth, are being targeted with cruelty — online, in our communities, and by politicians in Congress. I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too.
But we must remember that Pride was born at Stonewall in resistance, in protest, and in the belief that even in the face of fear, change is still possible.
**And as Pride Month comes to a close, I’m reminded again that we must continue to fight for what’s right.** To stay our values and our vision. And just as importantly, to keep believing that through the power of our proximity, we can bring more people along.
**But we won’t get there alone. It’s going to take all of us building a movement strong enough to meet this moment and carry us forward.**
[**So if you’re ready to do your part, please pitch in $5 before Monday’s FEC deadline. What we raise now will help us keep up the fight for a more just and kind world.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250627-1?refcode=em20250627-2133&amount=5&refcode2=2133_21716_ucXURe&akid=2133%2E21716%2EucXURe)
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250627-1?amount=5&refcode=em20250627-2133&refcode2=2133_21716_ucXURe&akid=2133%2E21716%2EucXURe)**
I know a better tomorrow is possible if we put in the work.
In solidarity and Happy Pride,
Sarah

President Donald Trump should win a Nobel Peace Prize, according to U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery).

Trump announced a ceasefire between Israel and Iran late Monday afternoon after days of bombings between the two countries and strikes by the United States on three of Iran's nuclear sites.

Britt said during an interview on Fox News Channel's "Hannity" on Monday night that Trump had "brought peace to a region that needed stability."

WASHINGTON D.C., DC — U.S. Senators Katie Britt (R-Ala.), Kevin Cramer (R-N.Dak.), Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), and several Senate Republican colleagues have introduced the Ground and Orbital Launched Defeat of Emergent Nuclear Destruction and Other Missile Engagements (GOLDEN DOME) Act. The legislation authorizes more than $23 billion to develop a modernized, layered homeland missile defense system designed to counter, detect, track, and defeat evolving threats, including hypersonic and cruise missiles. This initiative aligns with President Donald Trump’s January 27, 2025, executive order outlining a comprehensive missile defense strategy known as the Golden Dome.

### **When Billionaires Play House, the World Pays the Price**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/721cc721-14bc-454a-a055-55640dda38e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

`Full Blue Amp Subscription For Just $1.32/Week!`
_**We made the decision to give all who want it full access to Blue Amp for only $1.32 per week!**_
_**Get Truth corporate media ignores. And support our Creators Fund to construct a strong, viable, indy media ecosystem!**_
_**Amplify Good. Support Indy Media!**_
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.FwQS7FfbeEX_PDlmfs9Q4oD2lr_5gdSDET3Mfv1mbkI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=166981928)
We've been here before, haven't we? A billionaire throws a private, multi-gazillion‐dollar bash in a public space--and the spectacle somehow morphs into a fluffed-up narrative of "exclusivity" and "local benefits." **It 's damn near rote in the age of Trump.** But man, does the bullshit dissolve under the slightest bit of scrutiny.
Jeff Bezos isn't celebrating love; **he 's performing power**. He rented Venice--yes, we have monopolists renting whole cities--and we're calling it a wedding. But when an incel turned James Bond villain masquerading as a man--one who already controls more resources than many countries--rents a major city, it's a GD mating ritual.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f1b8b5-50f2-4bdb-83cc-543cc6ea6fd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Jeff Bezos, thinking he can be cool ...and she likes him for him_
I promise you this myopic mook doesn't see the outrage of Venetians, Americans and the world as regrettable. In fact, I'm quite sure it gives him the kinda dopamine high Elon needs to snort an Cybertruck to obtain. Jeff's living his best Trump life.
> Peacock spiders native to Australia have turned courtship into an art form. The tiny males, usually less than 5mm in size, perform elaborate dances to attract females. These performances involve raising and vibrating their colorfully patterned abdominal flaps, which resemble a peacock's fan, while simultaneously moving their third pair of legs in coordinated patterns.
Tiny, displaying abdominal flaps, a third pair of legs...that's Bezos all right.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db970806-a049-4bce-a867-4333fb237e26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Except he isn't trying to attract a female, he has his billions from our deranged, rapacious system of barely-regulated capitalism via bought-off clownfish in Congress. for that. No, this dance is a "fuck you" to everyone who somehow forgot that Bezos is better than us. And America has the Trumpian tax and regulation policies to prove it.
200 guests, 20-30 million euros in expenses, anchored by a $500 million yacht--which I'd pay good money to see someone go all Master and Commander on (while nobody's aboard, of course). Meanwhile, the locals are left to watch as canals are transformed into red-carpet lanes, and the city they live in every day is no longer their own because the Count of Corporate Conglomeration needs to show everyone who's boss.
Venetians are starving for housing, decent services, and a life they can afford. Instead, they're just a a photo op for a billionaire. Hell, he could feed them all for what he probalby paid for her lips. It's grotesque. As "No Space for Bezos" activists said loud and clear, "If you can rent Venice for your wedding you can pay more tax."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ed73bb7-6497-47bd-b166-9ffdc4330586?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_On the bright side, her lips can also be used as a flotation devic_ e
Yeah, I think I see this logic, considering during the presidencies of FDR, Truman and yes, Republican Dwight D. Eisenhower (when it was a whole different party--which is to say back when it's leadership didn't appear in the opening scene of "2001 a Space Odyssey.") these Presidents and Congress instituted a 90% top tax rate for bastards like Bezos. I mean, read this--I dare you not to find this even more repulsive:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2c85ad-31a9-4d1d-897b-ed6b4502058c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
More from this article:
> LISEP developed a "[Minimal Quality of Life Index](https://substack.com/redirect/2d3afdd4-d44d-4d1f-9988-dfc3150b64c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," which takes into account not only essentials, such as food and shelter, but the costs living a fulfilling life with a chance at upward mobility. Food costs in [the model](https://substack.com/redirect/c3ee7fc3-f8b5-4cd4-ab53-082a051e3c35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) include occasional trips to casual restaurants as well as the cost of hosting an annual holiday meal. The index factors in basic leisure costs, such as cable and streaming subscriptions, and trips to the six movies and two MLB games per year in the cheap seats.
> According to LISEP's analysis, most Americans don't meet that standard. In 2023, the bottom 60% of households by income fell well short of the threshold for a minimal quality of life.
This isn't isolated. From banners on bell towers to giant Bezos mannequins floating down the Grand Canal clutching dollar bills, **the message is clear: wealth should not confer the right to seize public space.**
Venetians are pushing back hard--blockades were threatened, banners splashed over iconic landmarks, and activists vowed to "make guests choke on their wedding cake." There's some great inverting of Marie Antoinette's thoughts in there.
Because, in Italy they understand what we need to re-learn from _our_ history, as Trump tries to sell off our public parks and little Bezos clones try to privatize everything. As Mr. Spock said in "Star Trek II, The Wrath of Khan," "The good of the many outweigh the good of the few. Or the one." A shorter synonym for that is _the public good_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a73afaa9-2006-45a9-a7aa-9d2152fa8f87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
`Full Blue Amp Subscription For Just $1.32/Week!`
_**We made the decision to give all who want it full access to Blue Amp for only $1.32 per week!**_
_**Get Truth corporate media ignores. And support our Creators Fund to construct a strong, viable, indy media ecosystem!**_

[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.FwQS7FfbeEX_PDlmfs9Q4oD2lr_5gdSDET3Mfv1mbkI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=166981928)
Of course, city officials swoon at the supposed "economic windfall." Mayor Brugnaro called it "an honor," eager to host corporate royalty. Meanwhile, renters are evicted, young people priced out of homes, and tourists are turned into traffic. Tell me again, how his self-indulgent, masturbatory celebration by a billionaire is the answer?
Some will insist, "They're giving back"--a million euros to Corila's research (Corila advances and assists with research on the Venice lagoon) and local vendors enjoying huge demand. But these are mere crumbs from a feast that will never be shared.
Bezos wields the wealth to shape policy, leverage tax loopholes and make cities paid props for his amusement. He gives with one hand, slaps you across the face with the other--turning overpriced airspace and canal routes into golden photo backdrops for his nice, quaint party.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/613323ed-a9c5-4f82-a58f-98d0615e9295?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the end, while Venetians fight to stay in their homes, Bezos casually buys a stage. Venice is his rented theater of the financially absurd, curated for luxury, shielded from scrutiny, all while global inequality reaches cruel and ultimately destabilizing levels. There's a helluva lot more arrogance in town than romance.
**This ostentatious, sham wedding is a statement: money writes history, and public space? Merely a acreage to be confiscate from the public by the highest bidder.**
**And yet --the protests matter. They're more than spectacle. They're a rebuke of billionaire impunity.** They stand up and say no--not to a man, but a system that measures a human's entire worth by the size of their wallet. Cured polio? Whether it's birthright citizenship, Miranda protections, or Social Security benefits--you're on your own unless you have connected people you can reach, or otherwise find a way to get through to someone, know exactly what to demand, how and when.

In a separate ruling last year, SCOTUS declared that law enforcement officers cannot be sued for failing to read you your Miranda rights. The Supreme Court just upheld Tennessee’s ban on gender-affirming care for minors—even though studies have shown that such care (which includes reversible puberty blockers) decreases the risk of suicide among trans youth by over 70%. This will make life even harder for people living in the 27 states that restrict gender-affirming care. To add to this crisis, Trump just announced that he’s shutting down the national LGBTQ+ suicide hotline—as calls to crisis hotlines have surged with Republicans in power. This is part of a coordinated effort across the country to systematically eradicate trans people. **Lawmakers from the state to federal level need to step up and defend their trans constituents.**[**Will you sign the petition today demanding Congress pass policies to protect trans people, rather than policies that will kill trans people?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTIG-U7IoCAEfZgmbtF5X05DQd4oDRkmsTaBWa3GHbQh615ezQkeK-hvzPNH8qvXaX7mnHJ6CxzU4PNgDLPmHtjBXT0bOjhqQdocgF7gL2hBs7_AeVeiL7m-UwjqqiH7BeOMSQvkUg0YLFnZVEROeDOgeg5x-X4YIVDbH7wUWTgGRsS52UOoEyLC1SLsfjnVbrzPZM6WshDMylPWPomabcy4MZCF2aJYAOdhB-Qz5t4M7l3PTSHzE3yr2dndXhnDjKvWJc6F2mtNyKXFrJ0gbU_Z4JecFmLFsCBqaPHZup0Dd9ELc7ahL4vmS0ApsGj3nzo7ZH6VJFnUN8eAigs3Ud6PNOP1W5KczmNHyWlCp-3d3drSPdv-Bvrd1ovoczq4BEGkfAPmyHkp51N9Sny7-w1GlqX6p56Mo1wXBjBNl-Wq4E4hp2kkUh9pBiSlkxlfjEA/4hp/alnGn-YvQNme1T6GvezG7w/h2/h001.M4nIwO7pL0oF2f2OaK6UNJJx3Cuatui-hMae5fuigjA) | [SIGN NOW](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTIG-U7IoCAEfZgmbtF5X05DQd4oDRkmsTaBWa3GHbQh615ezQkeK-hvzPNH8qvXaX7mnHJ6CxzU4PNgDLPmHtjBXT0bOjhqQdocgF7gL2hBs7_AeVeiL7m-UwjqqiH7BeOMSQvkUg0YLFnZVEROeDOgLoexPICaZxs_U-J_StPwKf2TFft842L8e-B3VFH7ffEhBGlr8QJ12RYfPktbV6tluQYaEkZqvjqooI579NcxVxf1YxkHI6wj7xQsYpHc2EfwqyFxHoP17m9-gwEyM0QLhavJKCYW3HZf2j1XsklPXs_hGnT7Bsj1iD_7iivibwHrtG13o1nJ9AjYQjhMpPdxg3sng6CDhgn6bZCHrYSndTa8ZP48lz-xHwGzfpYSq0s5knqQhddtX5aR6UqwnwytLxdk2XNrT2B2qsG1EEReBsLODJGUaOFrgjLes6SxtMQ/4hp/alnGn-YvQNme1T6GvezG7w/h3/h001.ZLIDODTE3pDUT6VUNUno84bLkFnvSS12bwBY9unm4HI)

We also must invest in LGBTQ+ community programs. For example, I’ve secured $1 million in federal funding to support the Ruth Ellis Center, which provides safe, affordable, identity-affirming housing for marginalized Black and brown Detroiters, especially LGBTQ+ young people.
I’m in the Equality Caucus in Congress, and I’ve introduced policies like:
* The _Justice For All Act_ , which would expand civil rights protections to prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
* The _Youth Homelessness Guaranteed Income Pilot Program Act_ , which would provide direct cash assistance to unhoused young people. At least 40% of unhoused youth are LGBTQ+.

And I’ve been proud to support policies such as:
* The _Transgender Health Care Access Act_ , which would expand access to live-saving, evidence-based gender-affirming care.
* The _Transgender Bill of Rights_ , a Congressional resolution calling on the federal government to protect the rights of transgender and nonbinary people, including ensuring that trans people have access to gender-affirming care.
* The _Equality Ac_ t, which would protect LGBTQ+ people from discrimination in jobs, housing, and public accommodations and guarantee them equal protection under the law.

As lawmakers across the country jeopardize trans people’s lives, we must urgently defend trans people and build support for pro-LGBTQ+ policies in Congress.
[**Please add your name to demand Congressmembers vote against any policies that would threaten trans people and other LGBTQ+ people’s rights and lives—and vote FOR policies like the**** _Justice for All Act_****, the**** _Transgender Health Care Access Act_****, and the**** _Transgender Bill of Rights_****.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTIG-U7IoCAEfZgmbtF5X05DQd4oDRkmsTaBWa3GHbQh615ezQkeK-hvzPNH8qvXaX7mnHJ6CxzU4PNgDLPmHtjBXT0bOjhqQdocgF7gL2hBs7_AeVeiL7m-UwjqqiH7BeOMSQvkUg0YLFnZVEROeDOjVBx1GuRUyUi69cFOMRCI-qbzKKtjfB1sJtPMZ7GbUsSoOccYjzLPz9tO8lC9VdWMIt7BdDEDZWmDbNXAmYXQXKxvsaWAx-aq3SA1dcBlxrknr0XquhKumgpiIguVCUlUvT253Akh5In2Yna_xJOEJSqpdkbPDtVwA1Xd4x0F1ucAk4vB0uy8D7TFueXPJz50cEdfBJJxuye48O8HaV1Tv_0Y81sbmX-M04BZWVfvFMKSRqHnzvm3jgMBqRymnfHXPgymgLWtpFXtzzWWCuJdEq25FIpLWGDrnxnSC4qxT4Q/4hp/alnGn-YvQNme1T6GvezG7w/h4/h001.FctpXd2olG6p4eTSDcVKxZmwvTH7cinEhcds98n91FQ)
Thank you so much for taking action and standing up for the LGBTQ+ community. It’s essential to keep doing so in this dangerous political climate that’s dehumanizing trans people and other marginalized communities. We must speak up to affirm that all life is sacred, that all of us deserve to exist and thrive, and that no one is disposable.
To anyone reading this who is trans or nonbinary: You deserve joy and safety, and you belong here. You have the right to be seen and loved for who you are. I value and respect you, and I promise to keep fighting for you.

clean_body: Congress must protect LGBTQ+ people’s rights, especially with increasing attacks. | | | Friend, This month and every month, I’m advocating for LGBTQ+ people’s rights. Earlier this month I had the joy of celebrating my LGBTQ+ loved ones and neighbors at Livonia Pride and Detroit’s Motor City Pride: As millions of us celebrate Pride around the country this month, Republicans are trying to undo essential protections for LGBTQ+ people, particularly transgender people. Soon, the Senate will vote on a budget bill that would take away medically necessary, lifesaving gender-affirming care from people on Medicaid. The Supreme Court just upheld Tennessee’s ban on gender-affirming care for minors—even though studies have shown that such care (which includes reversible puberty blockers) decreases the risk of suicide among trans youth by over 70%. This will make life even harder for people living in the 27 states that restrict gender-affirming care. To add to this crisis, Trump just announced that he’s shutting down the national LGBTQ+ suicide hotline—as calls to crisis hotlines have surged with Republicans in power. This is part of a coordinated effort across the country to systematically eradicate trans people. Lawmakers from the state to federal level need to step up and defend their trans constituents. | We also must invest in LGBTQ+ community programs. For example, I’ve secured $1 million in federal funding to support the Ruth Ellis Center, which provides safe, affordable, identity-affirming housing for marginalized Black and brown Detroiters, especially LGBTQ+ young people. I’m in the Equality Caucus in Congress, and I’ve introduced policies like: The Justice For All Act , which would expand civil rights protections to prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. The Youth Homelessness Guaranteed Income Pilot Program Act , which would provide direct cash assistance to unhoused young people. At least 40% of unhoused youth are LGBTQ+. And I’ve been proud to support policies such as: The Transgender Health Care Access Act , which would expand access to live-saving, evidence-based gender-affirming care. The Transgender Bill of Rights , a Congressional resolution calling on the federal government to protect the rights of transgender and nonbinary people, including ensuring that trans people have access to gender-affirming care. The Equality Ac t, which would protect LGBTQ+ people from discrimination in jobs, housing, and public accommodations and guarantee them equal protection under the law. As lawmakers across the country jeopardize trans people’s lives, we must urgently defend trans people and build support for pro-LGBTQ+ policies in Congress. Thank you so much for taking action and standing up for the LGBTQ+ community. It’s essential to keep doing so in this dangerous political climate that’s dehumanizing trans people and other marginalized communities. We must speak up to affirm that all life is sacred, that all of us deserve to exist and thrive, and that no one is disposable. To anyone reading this who is trans or nonbinary: You deserve joy and safety, and you belong here. You have the right to be seen and loved for who you are. I value and respect you, and I promise to keep fighting for you. In solidarity, Rashida P.S. Trans Lifeline runs a crisis hotline with trans operators providing peer support for trans and nonbinary people in need. Two of those investigations led to formal charges by the Indiana Supreme Court Disciplinary Commission. **State Rep. Ed. DeLaney: “We’re paying four law firms close to half a million dollars so that Todd Rokita can keep his law license and stay in office,” he said. “That’s a campaign expense — not something the public should have to fund.”** Mike Braun admitted this week that Hoosiers paid over $1 million for execution drugs over the past year, and that unused doses expired before they could be used. _$600,000 was spent on drugs that expired and were never used._ This all took place while the media reported on a $1 billion shortfall for Indiana Medicaid, forcing Hoosier children and seniors onto waitlists. Republicans specifically did this to control the freedom Hoosier families had to make decisions about their own body. We want Hoosier women to have the freedom to make their own medical decisions without the government getting involved in the most private aspects of their lives. Republicans are moving quickly towards criminalizing women seeking abortion care in states across the country. Even this year, Indiana Republicans [filed a bill](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110394287/554203762/18848444?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OWNmYjZjYS1hYzUzLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=CUp4UIJ1N2NoQmHdmF0Kt7D18-UW-09IFP2Nk8tlSv8=&emci=d936dda7-aa53-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=89cfb6ca-ac53-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=4925535) to criminally charge women in Indiana, but thanks to united Democratic opposition, it did not pass. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. body:
And Alexandria is different, too.
#
Can we be real with you for a moment?
We understand that a constant stream of emails asking for a contribution can sometimes get on your nerves. That’s okay. Real people wrote this email, we get them as well. We understand how people can get frustrated. _But let us explain why this is vital._
When we’re asking for your support, we don’t expect every person to give. But we ask because we know that when you can support the cause, you will. That’s how this transformative movement works.**It’s a whole lot of people doing their part to make something great.**
[We’re just 3 days away from our end-of-quarter deadline, and we’re hoping to hit our fundraising targets before then. The only way we can is through the support of small-dollar donors chipping in whatever they can. If you can, will you make a $3 contribution — or $5, or anything you can — right now? It’ll go a long way.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250627-2.mZK8uz&refcode=em20250627-9186-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9186%2E2526796%2En72fsq)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250627-2.mZK8uz&refcode=em20250627-9186-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=20&akid=9186%2E2526796%2En72fsq)**
We’re not exaggerating: most members of Congress fuel their reelection campaigns by dedicating hours of their time asking rich donors for $500, $1000, or even $3300 donations.
**Alexandria is different.** This whole movement is fueled by online contributions like the ones we’re asking for in this email. With these contributions, we’ve built a campaign that is...
1. Raising resources, recruiting volunteers, and making calls to help elect progressive allies across Congress, and build a progressive majority.
2. Reaching out to communities across NY-14 and the country to spread awareness about the Green New Deal, how to influence local, state, and federal leaders, and more.
3. Raising money for community relief organizations, closing critical resources gaps that the federal government has left unfilled.
4. Working day and night to reelect AOC, defeat our Republican opponents, and show the world what we can do.

[If this movement is the model of what you want in our politics, please donate today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250627-2.mZK8uz&refcode=em20250627-9186-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=9186%2E2526796%2En72fsq)
Thanks for reading,
Team AOC
